Age Group — Active vs New Users
This section shows the age groups of active and new users.

More than 90% of users have no age information. Among users with known ages, 25–34 is the largest group. The next larger groups are 18–24 and 35–44. Users aged 45+ represent a smaller portion of the known data. The 25–34 age group also matches the findings from the separate user survey.

Continue designing for a fast, convenient, mobile-friendly shopping experience. Use the existing 25–34 persona as a useful reference for current UX work. Keep accessibility in mind for older users as well. Continue improving the quality of age data.

Most Users Are Still Guests The difference between registered users and active users is significant. This likely explains why age and gender information is missing for more than 90% of users. So, these are not necessarily separate problems. They may be connected to the same issue: most users are not identified. 2. Web and Android Have Different Roles New users mainly come through Web, while active users are more heavily represented on Android. This suggests that Web may be the main entry point, while Android may play a bigger role in continued usage. However, this should be tested before assuming that moving users from Web to Android will automatically improve retention. 3. The 25–34 Age Group Is a Useful Direction The 25–34 group is the largest known age group in the analytics data. This is also similar to the separate survey findings, so we can use the existing 25–34 persona as a reasonable reference for current design work. 4. Tamil Nadu Is the Core Market The user data clearly shows that Annachy has a strong Tamil Nadu customer base, with Chennai leading by a large margin. This means regional needs should be considered when planning UX improvements. 5. Some Data Needs to Be Cleaned Up There are differences between some of the reported user numbers. There are also users with “Not Set” locations. Before using this data for major business decisions, the analytics team should confirm that all sections are using the same definitions and date ranges.

This section shows which platforms users are using: Android, Web, iOS, and PWA.

Web accounts for 61.33% of new users. Android accounts for 55.29% of active users. This shows a clear difference between new users and active users. iOS usage is currently very low. PWA data is not available.

Improve the Web experience for first-time users. Make product discovery and first purchase easier on Web. Test an app-install message for users who are already engaged on Web. Check whether Android users have better retention than Web users. Understand why iOS usage is very low. Check whether PWA could be useful for users who don't want to install an app.

Observation: New users mainly come through Web, while active users are mainly on Android. User Impact: The first experience happens mainly on Web, but continued engagement appears stronger on Android. UX Opportunity: Improve the Web-to-Android journey and test whether moving engaged users to the app improves retention.

This section gives us an overall view of Annachy’s users during the 90-day period from 19 May to 18 August 2026. It covers registered users, active users, new users, returning users, total users, and first-time users.
Annachy has 2.72 lakh registered users, compared with 17.23 lakh active users.
This means a large number of people are using Annachy without creating an account.
There is a small mismatch between the New Users + Returning Users and the reported Total Users.
There is also a difference between New Users and First-Time Users.
These differences should be checked with the analytics/data team before using the numbers for important business decisions.
Show registration at useful moments, such as after adding a product to the cart.
Explain the benefit of signing in instead of simply asking users to register.
Benefits could include: Saving the cart Faster checkout Order tracking Saved addresses Viewing order history
Keep the registration process short and simple.

91.72% of active users have their gender marked as unknown. 89.74% of new users also have their gender marked as unknown. Among users whose gender is known, male users are higher than female users. The male/female pattern is fairly similar between new and active users

This section shows where Annachy users are located based on active and new users.

Chennai is the largest market by a significant margin. Coimbatore is the second-largest city. Madurai and Salem also have a strong presence. Most of the major cities in the data are in Tamil Nadu. Bengaluru and Hyderabad are the main markets outside Tamil Nadu. Bengaluru has a slightly stronger share of new users compared with its active-user share.

Prioritize Tamil Nadu when planning regional UX improvements. Consider local language and communication needs. Look at regional delivery expectations. Explore city-specific offers or product recommendations. Understand whether Bengaluru and Hyderabad users behave differently. Fix the “Not Set” location data so future analysis becomes more accurate.
